positive: Early-layer, mostly token-level. Tokens like 'incorporate/incorporating/Incorporate', 'personalize', Arabic prefix tokens (ح, الت), Chinese 人力; plausibly closing-quote/punctuation contexts (output promotes ."), "), "]) ) so may fire just before closing quotes/parentheses in quoted speech or code strings.
negative: Tokens like 'recursively', 'emit', 'mitt', 'incremento', 'выполнения', httpClient, Chinese procedural words (严格按照, 下发); code/procedural verbs such as execute/emit/run.

positive: Embedded/hardware programming contexts: EEPROM, firmware, bootloader, flash memory, Arduino, FPGA, microcontroller (单片机), memory/memcpy, battery; fires on the token right before 'flash'/'program'/'programming' would be predicted (e.g. 'write the firmware to...', 'upload/flash the'). Strongest on 'firmware', 'EEPROM', 'bootloader', 'memory'.
negative: Weakly negative on hardware-adjacent but non-memory terms: 'wire', 'interrupt', 'Motor', 'voltage', 'layer', 'Smart', 'Media', 'Control'; also projection/director/score contexts.

positive: Contexts predicting the number 'three' (or thirty/ten): counting/enumeration, 'there are three...', '有三个', math word problems listing counts; also possibly 'sub' prefixes. Closing-quote punctuation tokens (”， ”،) directly.
negative: Hedging/uncertainty contexts where 'possibly/likely/maybe' (可能, likely, presumably) would follow; token 'presumably' itself; sentence-start '.The'; code identifiers (statusCode, ServletContext).

positive: Agriculture/horticulture/animal husbandry text about breeds, varieties, cultivars: 'species', 'breeds', 'habitat', 'endemic', 'nursery', 'hardy', 'breeding', 品种/繁殖/饲养; fires when the next word is likely 'variety/strain/breed/cultivation/adapted'. Also household/domestic contexts (domestic animals, installed).
negative: Biology/microbiology lab contexts: 'infected', 'organism', 'genome', 'assay', 'immune', 'reproductive', 'propagated', 'stalk', hybridization (杂交), inoculation (接种); also physics/electrical terms (ion, charge, capacitor) gate off.

positive: Weak early-layer token detector: 'willing', 'background', 'solid', 'hard', 'easy', 'newspaper', 'tractor/ATV', Chinese 人/人对/可以作为/主要为.
negative: Closing brackets/quote clusters in code ("))), ")(, "],", '}).), Chinese boilerplate like 给我留言/咨询我/依法追究责任/在新的一年里, '谓语'; temperature units (°F, Fahrenheit) gate off.

positive: Time/ordinal words: 'second' (esp. 'second' as ordinal or time unit), 'month', 'year', 'December', 'few', 'soon', 'almost'; Portuguese 'muito', 'certa'; 'automobile', 'segment', 'tolerance'. Likely fires in 'a few seconds/months' type phrases.
negative: 'un-' / 'uni-' prefix tokens and short function fragments: '-un', 'un', 'UN', 'una', 'ut', 'u', 'd', 'pur', 'dia', 'separ', 'gener'; wildcard/asterisk tokens (.*, ******) and HTML '</'.

positive: Weak: 'Process/process', 'AH', 'bread', 'stone' (石头), Polish/Dutch question words (jakie, welke), Russian 'подготовки'.
negative: Configuration / location words: 'config', '-config', '_config', 'Config', 'configuration'; 'where/Where', 'где', 'حيث'; 'await'; pronoun 'it/It'; 'split', 'src'. Programming config files and relative clauses 'where...'.

positive: Fires after 'etc', 'others/他人/别人', on hedge-ish tokens; contexts where a noun rather than 'the/same/most/latter' follows, e.g. after 'of the' constructions? Likely positive on 'etc.', 'vs' gate tokens, Chinese 一直/少量/一切/类似问题, '-of'.
negative: Strongly negative on/around determiner 'the' (all variants) and 'their', 'an' since up is low there with gate positive; also 'vs', 'versus', 'despite', 'although', 'when', 'refers', 'nobody'. Predicts suppressing superlative/abstract nouns after 'the' (same, most, latter, entire, original, greatest).

positive: Hyphen-prefixed tokens in compound words or command-line flags: '-sh', '-int', '-var', '-and', '-one', '-set', '-or', '-th', '-col' (e.g. 'well-known', 'two-thirds', 'non-...', CLI flags like -f -t). Fires on the hyphenated continuation, suppressing another hyphen next.
negative: Bare hyphen/non-breaking hyphen tokens and CSS/class-name style hyphen suffixes: '-', '‑', '‐', '-like', '-data', '-container', '-top', '-placeholder', '-content', '-info', '-outline', '-looking'; zero-width chars (\u200c); HTML class names like 'btn-outline', 'data-...'.

positive: Relative-clause and complementizer contexts: tokens after 'that', 'which', 'whose', 'who', 'yang', 'الذي', 'که', 'που'; question words (哪, nào, này); 'never', 'wrong', 'seen'. Also predicts code endings like '):' and '":' (Python def/dict lines).
negative: Direct tokens 'that', 'required', 'requested', 'sought', 'indicated', 'pictured', 'attempted', 'implements', 'you', 'object', 'Class' - past participles in reduced relative clauses ('as requested', 'the item pictured'). Also math trig tokens (*sin, *cos, *width) gate off.
